basis: Hosted Foundation runtime run 36958570357 (check-run 110686941886) @4c0664a on main, 2026-10-02, correctly failed closed (Restricted policy regressions: hosted-full-stack-dependency-audit, exit 1) after a batch of new pypdf advisories published since the 2026-10-01 green baseline. The GitHub Advisory and OSV APIs were unreachable from the triage environment at round time (401/egress-blocked), so the live match set was re-derived independently: every package@version of a fresh local resolution of the pinned dependency union (frappe@988e54f3c4c291e2077a83809663f123731abe76, erpnext@4048fb70e14d1843956fcdabb7c3cca75a1cbcdd, education@93bc7075753369457919720690f80c6d2207b5f2, hrms@a4768b441cff346def505e27f2a2229ee1e05b9b, payments@cca07d9f9392e2ea0e521c5975151db9e4b6c321; 159-distribution venv, mysqlclient==2.2.7 added at its pinned exact version) was queried against the PyPI JSON API (OSV-backed 'vulnerabilities' feed), and triaged with the repository's own advisory_triage.disposition_for_finding against the 2026-09-23 register and every earlier delta. That left exactly this one package, py:pypdf@6.15.0, with 16 uncovered records: 8 GHSA ids (CVE-2026-102993..103000) plus their 8 PYSEC mirrors (PYSEC-2026-4153..4160). The run's remaining pypdf matches (GHSA-23w6-3w8w-8484, GHSA-763m-79hh-57f2, GHSA-jp53-mhqp-8xcg and PYSEC-2026-3910/3911/3913) are covered by the 2026-09-23 register, and the run's pyjwt/oauthlib PYSEC-4xxx mirrors are covered through their GHSA/CVE aliases. The npm side was checked against the npm bulk advisory endpoint for the run's visible package list: all entries closed, no regressions. Reachability was traced in the pinned source trees listed in the per-finding evidence, plus the owned apps.. The first round (pypdf) was verified in CI: the run's STACK-ADVISORY-UNTRIAGED diagnostic annotations (added in d1b4e3f) then showed the remaining failure set was 15 further records - PYSEC-2026-4113/4114 (py:oauthlib@3.3.1) and PYSEC-2026-4140..4152 (py:pyjwt@2.13.0) - PyPA mirror records of 15 GHSA advisories already triaged in the 2026-09-29, 2026-09-30-2, 2026-09-30-3 and 2026-10-01 deltas. The OSV feed carries these PyPA records without the GHSA cross-reference the PyPI feed shows (the PyPI feed confirms the pairing, e.g. PYSEC-2026-4114 = GHSA-xpv3-w29h-x7cv / CVE-2026-49265; PYSEC-2026-4113 pairs with GHSA-hj66-6f7g-4r5v / CVE-2026-49264 by the 1:1 package-batch correspondence in the same run), so they triaged as untriaged despite the identical underlying vulnerabilities being dispositioned. Each entry below carries the same disposition as its mirrored GHSA with the prior analysis cited. Their CVE aliases are all already covered, so no alias is re-listed (the loader fails closed on redefinition).

advisories.summary: pypdf: long runtimes reading a PDF with long indirect object headers not terminated by whitespace
advisories.runtime_disposition_evidence: Reached whenever the reader resolves indirect objects (read_object_header, pypdf/_reader.py:614): pdf_contains_js does so at reader construction and again while walking the whole object tree for /JS keys. The only pinned paths that construct a reader over attacker-controlled bytes are File.check_content -> pdf_contains_js (frappe/core/doctype/file/file.py:477-478; frappe/utils/pdf.py:449-461) on any uploaded PDF, and the System-Manager-only bank-statement import (erpnext bank_statement_import_log.py:964-975; that doctype's sole permission role is System Manager per its fixture, which no product staff role carries). Uploads are body-capped at the WSGI layer before any parsing: frappe/app.py:234-238 sets request.max_content_length = get_max_file_size() (System Settings max_file_size, else frappe's 25 MB default; the product does not override), bounding the parse cost. The surface requires an authenticated user and the deployment is tailnet-only (D13/D15; no internet exposure). Impact is availability-only (bounded long runtimes on one worker request); no data exposure or privilege escalation.
advisories.fix_path: Official Frappe release carrying pypdf >= 6.18.0. Pinned frappe@988e54f pins pypdf==6.15.0 - EXTERNAL/UPSTREAM BLOCKED, unchanged posture.

The per-finding reachability analysis for GHSA-gvp8-978c-rx2q in advisory-delta-2026-10-01 applies unchanged: The defect mutates a caller-supplied options mapping when verify_signature is falsy, so it only matters when application code reuses ONE options object across two or more jwt.decode()/decode_complete() calls (the advisory states calls that build a fresh options dict per call are unaffected; signature verification itself is unaffected). Repository-wide search of all five pinned upstream trees and the owned apps finds the complete jwt surface in frappe@988e54f3 only: frappe/oauth.py:324 jwt.encode (no options); frappe/oauth.py:446-454 jwt.decode with an inline literal options={verify_signature: False, verify_aud: False}; frappe/oauth.py:467-475 jwt.decode with a separate inline literal options={verify_exp: False}; frappe/utils/oauth.py:200 jwt.decode with an inline literal options={verify_signature: False}. Every call constructs its own dict at the call site; there is no module-level, class-level, instance-level or shared options object, so the mutated dict of the unverified-parse call is discarded and can never reach a verifying call (the second oauth.py decode already disables verify_exp explicitly and uses a different dict object). erpnext, education, payments, hrms and the owned apps (toefl_house, foundation_security) contain zero jwt imports or calls. The per-finding reachability analysis for GHSA-jwrc-g2q2-pq5p in advisory-delta-2026-09-30-3 applies unchanged: In pyjwt 2.13.0 is_pem_format has exactly one caller, HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key(key) (jwt/algorithms.py:331); it inspects the KEY argument, never the token. Across all five pinned trees and the owned apps only frappe@988e54f3c4c291e2077a83809663f123731abe76 uses PyJWT, with keys: oauth.py:324 jwt.encode key=OAuth Client client_secret (server-generated); oauth.py:467 jwt.decode key=client_secret read from the OAuth Client record; utils/oauth.py:200 flow.client_secret (admin-configured Social Login Key) with verify_signature False.
